message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Deploy

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 22.x
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Setup Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v6

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Build with vite
        run: npm run build

      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5
        with:
          path: ./dist

  deploy:
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: build
    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v5
",
  "rationale": "Apply P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (bound jobs with a custom timeout). The measured experiment example shows adding timeout-minutes: 5 to a job kept all successes (3/3) while cutting median elapsed 41s to 30s (26.8% savings), and the pattern reports vm_time_reduction_percent free 12.9 / paid 8.1. The precondition is met: CI history shows representative successful runs completing in roughly 35s, so a 5-minute bound gives generous headroom and will not truncate valid builds or deploys. The change only adds timeout-minutes: 5 to the build and deploy jobs; all triggers, steps, permissions, concurrency cancellation, and required coverage are preserved, with no weakened permissions, secrets, new network access, or publishing changes.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508", "pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT"]
}
